- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to counteract bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reverting trends; add a 1–2% upward bias in early forecast periods if recent price is above 70.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; adjust forecast downward if sentiment turns negative within 5 days of forecast start.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.27 or +0.49 spikes, model tends to overreact; apply a 5–10% downward correction to avoid overfitting to sentiment momentum.
